info.desc: Funeral is the debut full-length album by Canadian indie rock band Arcade Fire, released on September 14, 2004 in North America by Merge Records and on February 28, 2005 in Europe by Rough Trade Records. It was given its title because several band members had recently lost members of their families: Régine Chassagne's grandmother died in June 2003, Win and William Butler's grandfather (swing musician Alvino Rey) in March 2004, and Richard Reed Parry's aunt in April 2004. Preliminary recordings for Funeral were made during the course of a week in August 2003 at the Hotel2Tango in Montreal, Quebec, and .

podcast.body: This album garnered worldwide critical attention and, despite Merge Records' previous struggles, led to the band's explosion in popularity. Its success helped Arcade Fire become one of the most talked-about and awarded bands of the 21st century. "First, they had this EP and then an album called Funeral, and it caught the attention of critics worldwide... then Arcade Fire comes along with Funeral, and things just blew up."

podcast.body: Recorded quickly in about a week in the summer of 2003 at Hotel to Tango studio in Montreal and finished by early 2004, this album was released on September 14, 2004. It was titled "Funeral" due to the deaths of several band members' relatives (grandfathers, grandmothers, aunts) during its creation. The album received immediate critical acclaim and attention, leading to club shows, festival appearances globally, a Time Magazine cover, and friendships with figures like David Bowie. It became the best-selling album ever for Merge Records at the time, garnering three Grammy and three Brit Award nominations, and a Juno for Songwriters of the Year, making it the most significant debut album of the decade. "The band called it funeral, because so many of the band's relatives died during its making."

This album is part of what is considered their "sacred trilogy" of first albums, which are now modern classics, having peaked in the early 21st century's alternative music scene. podcast.body: This album contains the song "Haiti," which is accompanied by a video that was shot entirely on location in Haiti. Regine Chassagne maintains a blog on the band's website detailing the group's experiences related to this country. "Haiti, from the funeral album, if you're interested in going deeper, Regina blogs about the band's experiences at the group's website."
